messages:
maya: Heads up — after the AZ failover a subset of pods in us-east-1a lost egress to S3 via the interface VPC endpoint. App logs show 504s and occasional "No route to host". Other AZs (1b/1c) look fine. Anyone touching privatelink/RT associations?

aj: Which endpoint ID + subnet/ENI? Also paste a failing curl from a pod if you can.

maya: endpoint id vpce-0a1b2c3d4e5f6g7, ENI eni-0f1e2d3c4b5a6, affected subnet subnet-0a11. From a failing pod:
```
# curl -v http://s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/bucket/foo -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}
'
* Rebuilt URL to: http://s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/bucket/foo
*   Trying 172.31.12.45...
* connect to 172.31.12.45 port 80 failed: Connection timed out
* Failed to connect to s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com port 80: Connection timed out
000
```

Also getting these from app: "socket.gaierror: [Errno 101] Network is unreachable"

liam: Can you paste `aws ec2 describe-vpc-endpoints --vpc-endpoint-ids vpce-0a1b2c3d4e5f6g7` output (sanitized) and `aws ec2 describe-route-tables --filters Name=association.subnet-id,Values=subnet-0a11`?

maya: quick bits:
```
VpcEndpointId: vpce-0a1b2c3d4e5f6g7
State: available
SubnetIds: [subnet-0a11, subnet-0a22, subnet-0a33]
NetworkInterfaceIds: [eni-0f1e2d3c4b5a6, eni-0a2b3c4d5e6f7, eni-0b2c3d4e5f6a7]
RouteTableIds: [rtb-aaaa1111]  # this is the route table that should be associated with the subnets
```
But `describe-route-tables` against subnet-0a11 shows it's still associated to an old rtb-bbbb2222 (leftover from a trunking change).

aj: aha. So the endpoint ENI is in subnet-0a11 but the subnet is pointing at a different route table that doesn't have the endpoint route/assoc. If the route table doesn't have an explicit association to the endpoint, traffic won't go to the VPCE. That explains AZ-only impact if only that subnet's RT is stale.

liam: two quick checks: security group egress on the ENI (allow 443 to S3 prefix list?), and make sure source/dest check is enabled/disabled? Also NACLs + ephemeral ports. But most likely RT assoc drift.

infra-bot: Automated check: VPCE subnet assoc mismatch detected for vpce-0a1b2c3d4e5f6g7: subnet-0a11 -> rtb-bbbb2222 (expected rtb-aaaa1111). Alert created: #INC-8271

aj: You can fix by associating the correct route table to subnet-0a11: `aws ec2 associate-route-table --route-table-id rtb-aaaa1111 --subnet-id subnet-0a11` (this is safe for us since rtb-aaaa1111 is the intended one). Would also re-create the subnet->rt association via IaC after.

maya: doing it now.

sre-oncall: quick heads-up, after you flip RT associations, also run `sudo conntrack -D` on the nodes in that AZ (or restart kube-proxy) — conntrack can hold dead TCP 4-tuple state pointing at the old path. Might see 30s-120s recovery otherwise.

(30s later)

maya: associated rtb-aaaa1111 -> subnet-0a11. pods started recovering. 95% success now, a few kept failing until conntrack flush.

liam: follow-up tickets: 1) add a check in infra runbooks to validate VPC endpoint route-table consistency across AZs and alert if any subnet points to an unexpected RT; 2) automation to re-run associations as part of AZ failover playbook; 3) postmortem on why IaC drift left rtb-bbbb2222.

aj: Agreed. Also add a small k8s probe test during failover to hit the VPCE from each AZ.

maya: thanks everyone :tada: — marking incident resolved. Will put remediation PR for Terraform drift detection.

sre-oncall: resolved in #INC-8271, closing alert.
